Container.Name: Tinyfin API
Container.Overview: Jellyfin-compatible media server in one Go binary, API only: no bundled web UI, MIT image with no GPL assets. Use it with the Jellyfin mobile, TV or Kodi clients, or when another web UI is already served elsewhere.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: jellyfin media server movies tv shows transcode ffmpeg nvenc emby alternative api
Container.Description:
Tinyfin speaks the Jellyfin HTTP API, so unchanged Jellyfin clients work against it: the mobile and TV apps, the Kodi add-on, Findroid, Infuse. It is a clean-room implementation, not a fork, and the state lives in one SQLite file.
This is the **API-only** variant: the image is MIT and ships no `jellyfin-web` assets, so there is no web UI at `/web/`. Install the `Tinyfin` template instead if you want the browser UI bundled. Yes, you can also point an external `jellyfin-web` build at this server.
### First start
There is no web wizard here. Create the admin user and add libraries with a Jellyfin client, or with the Jellyfin API (`/User`, `/Library/VirtualFolders`). Libraries point at `/media`, which is mounted read-only on purpose, because Tinyfin never writes to your files.
### Metadata and scanning
`TINYFIN_TMDB_API_KEY` is optional. Without it the scan catalogues files and reads local NFO and artwork, with no online metadata. The scanner skips a file when size and mtime did not change; `TINYFIN_SCAN_FORCE_PROBE` re-probes everything.
### Container notes
- The image is distroless: no shell, no curl, no wget. It cannot carry a Docker healthcheck. Check `GET /System/Info/Public` from outside instead. - The image runs as uid 65532 by default. The template adds `--user 99:100` so appdata stays `nobody:users` like every other Unraid container. - `/data` holds `tinyfin.db`, `tinyfin.db.images`, `tinyfin.db.server-id` and `log/`. Keep it on a path you back up. A fresh instance starts empty. - NVIDIA hardware transcoding: add `--runtime=nvidia -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all -e NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=compute,video,utility` to the extra parameters and install the Unraid NVIDIA driver plugin. - The container port is 8096, the Jellyfin default, so a client only needs the new address. If Jellyfin or Emby already owns 8096 on this server, pick another host port.
### Status
Release `0.x`. Phases 0 to 3 are done and were tested against real clients. Coverage is honest, not complete: check `docs/COVERAGE.md` in the project before you rely on a feature. Live TV, DVR, DLNA, offline mobile sync and a plugin loader are out of scope for 0.x.
Project documentation: https://github.com/rafaelvieiras/tinyfin

Config.Name: API port
Config.Description: HTTP port for the Jellyfin API. Clients use the same port they would use against Jellyfin.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: SQLite database, generated images, server id and logs. Keep it on a path you back up.

Config.Name: Media
Config.Description: Your media, read-only. Libraries inside Tinyfin are added with the /media path.

Config.Name: TMDB API key
Config.Description: Enables online metadata. Empty: catalog-only scan using local NFO and artwork.

Config.Name: Scan concurrency
Config.Description: Scan workers per library. Raise it for a slow remote filesystem.

Config.Name: Library parallelism
Config.Description: Libraries scanned at the same time.

Config.Name: Timezone
Config.Description: Container timezone for log timestamps. Empty: UTC.
